changelog: Insert a short Core Principle after C5 forbidding cuts that separate core predicates from required arguments or that split enumerations/verb phrases; this directly addresses the primary finding about harmful internal splits.
findings: The prompt over-penalizes sentence‑initial short openers (The/It/In/short adverbials/pronouns), avoiding early cuts that are often safe and valuable for very-short latency.
The prompt is now too eager to insert internal cuts that detach required predicates/arguments or fragment enumerations, which degrades mid‑length cohesion.

edits.was: - Long noun groups and multiword modifiers accumulate referential content toward
edits.now: - Preserve predicate–argument and enumerations: do not cut between a core predic

diagnosis.why: Inserting the core-principle blocked cuts that split predicates/arguments and enumerations, so the scorer stopped keeping many short internal splits (improving the smallest latency bins ≤3 and ≤5). However the constraint caused the kept-cut budget to be reallocated in mid-length pieces (bins ≤7 and ≤10), producing more cuts that split subjects/verbs or other heads and so made many mid-length cases worse.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should preserve the benefit of preventing internal predicate/argument and enumeration splits for short pieces while avoiding wholesale reallocation of cuts that creates new subject–verb or head splits in mid-length examples.
